newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Chinese demand for NZ wool seen improving.
newsitem.headline: Chinese demand for NZ wool seen improving.

text.p: Prospects are looking strong for improvement in Chinese demand for New Zealand wool in the 1996/97 season, Wools of New Zealand said on Wednesday.
International apparel manager Strath Stewart said low hand-knitting yarn stocks and an early start to the season boded well for China's wool purchases.

Wools of NZ plans to launch its Fernmark brand on the Chinese apparel market on November 28. It said it wants to capitalise on a still buoyant Chinese domestic economy and a range of favourable domestic demands.
Stewart said China would continue to be an important market for New Zealand wool but it was frustrating that it should be characterised by dishonoured and re-negotiated supply contracts.
